evidence: Traupman 18: fairly well, mediocriter quidem valeō
terms.comment: Lewis & Short has mediocriter “moderately, tolerably” as classical (corpus mediocriter aegrum, Cic. Tusc. 3.22), but not with valeō; the phrase is Traupman’s.

terms.gloss: given for “things are going fairly well”
evidence: Traupman 99, 322: things are going fairly well, agitur satis
Cic. Att. 4.15.9: pugnātur ācriter: agitur tamen satis (Lewis & Short s.v. satis)
terms.comment: Classically satis agere is to have one’s hands full, to be hard pressed, and Lewis & Short reads Cicero’s agitur tamen satis so: “still, it is a hard struggle” (see trouble). For “fairly well”, Variē or Mediocriter (above).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 15, 18.
